****SOC Case Report****

**Case ID:** POM-3 — Credential Harvesting
**Severity:** High
**Detection Date:** 2025-10-14 18:19:38 UTC
**Detection Source:** Email
**Affected User:** finance-grp@example.com

**Detection Details:**
A credential-harvesting email spoofing payrollvendor@externalvendor.com was delivered to finance-grp@example.com. Microsoft Defender for Office flagged an SPF fail and a malicious URL, which was zapped by Microsoft Defender. No traffic was observed to the domain but the SOC confirmed that the domain exhibited credential harvesting behavior. SOC added the domain, IP address and hosting provider to its Threat Intelligence platform, which is integrated with Splunk. No evidence of compromise was observed. SOC shared this information with other components.

**Incident Timeline:**
- (2025-10-14 18:19:38 UTC) — Malicious email flagged by Microsoft Defender for Office due to SPF failure and a malicious URL.

****Triage:****
- **Host:** finance-grp@example.com
- **Source Name:** Porkbun
- **User Info:** assets@demo.com
- **Case URL:** https://swimlane.assets.demosite.com:443/account/f3349d75-6783-4e74-9c3c-76f396e19e9a/tenant/679bd671-c2de-4d6d-b1f0-91f0d65406ce/record/aEza_JJOovvdR3rIX/aPzFLQF0bTomHst_h

**Actions Taken:**
- The malicious email was automatically removed from user inboxes (Zapped) by Microsoft Defender.
- The SOC manually analyzed the suspicious domain and confirmed it was hosting a credential harvesting page.
- The malicious domain, associated IP address, and hosting provider were added to the Threat Intelligence platform for future blocking.
- Findings were shared with other relevant security and IT components.

**Recommended Remediations:**
- **Block Malicious Indicators:** The domain, IP address, and hosting provider associated with the phishing campaign were blocked to prevent future communication.
- **Preserve Evidence:** The original phishing email was preserved as an artifact. This allows for deeper analysis of tactics and for the extraction of Indicators of Compromise (IOCs) to improve security tool configurations.

**Artifacts:**
- **Network/Host:** finance-grp@example.com
- **Account/User:**
    - Recipient: finance-grp@example.com
    - Spoofed Sender: payrollvendor@externalvendor.com

****Tools & Queries Run:****

**Splunk Correlation Query:**
```splunk
index=azure sourcetype=Defender (spf_result="fail" or dkim="fail") and subject="*Payroll*" | table _time, sender, recipients, subject, src_ip, url
```

**MITRE ATT&CK Mapping:**
- **T1566 - Phishing:** This technique was used by the adversary to send a spoofed email to the target organization, which served as the initial delivery mechanism for the attack.
- **T1566.002 - Spearphishing Link:** The email contained a malicious link intended to lure users into clicking it, which is a classic method for directing victims to credential harvesting sites.
- **T1588 - Obtain Capabilities:** This technique is relevant as the adversary acquired the necessary infrastructure (domains, hosting) to carry out the phishing attack.

**Lessons Learned / Actions Taken:**
A credential-harvesting email spoofing payrollvendor@externalvendor.com was delivered to finance-grp@example.com. Microsoft Defender for Office flagged an SPF fail and a malicious URL, which was zapped by Microsoft Defender. No traffic was observed to the domain but the SOC confirmed that the domain exhibited credential harvesting behavior. SOC added the domain, IP address and hosting provider to its Threat Intelligence platform, which is integrated with Splunk. No evidence of compromise was observed. SOC shared this information with other components.
